quizName: DMV Practice Test #5 30 Questions • Passing Score 25

questions.question: What best protects your eyes from wind?
questions.correctAnswerText: Goggles
questions.explanation: Goggles and face shields protect your eyes from wind. Windshields, eyeglasses, and sunglasses do not.

questions.question: Your lane position should help you:

options.text: Communicate your intentions to other drivers.
Travel to your destination as quickly as possible.
Stay in the blind spots of other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Communicate your intentions to other drivers.
questions.explanation: Your lane position should protect your lane and show other drivers what you plan to do next.

questions.question: Making eye contact with other drivers:

options.text: Guarantees they will yield to you.
Does not mean they see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean they see you.
questions.explanation: Do not rely on eye contact. A driver may look directly at you and still not notice you.

questions.question: To swerve, you should:

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
Press the handgrip in the opposite direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: Press the handgrip on the side you want to go. To swerve left, press the left handgrip, then the right to recover. To swerve right, press the right handgrip, then the left.

questions.question: To lean a motorcycle when turning, you should:

options.text: Press the handgrip opposite the direction of the turn.
Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle must lean to turn. Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn to make the motorcycle lean that way.

questions.question: Where is the horn button usually located?
questions.correctAnswerText: By the left handgrip
questions.explanation: Know the location of all your motorcycle's controls before you ride. The horn button is usually next to the left handgrip.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Do both at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one, then the other.
questions.explanation: Do each action separately. Brake then swerve, or swerve then brake. Do not do both at the same time.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, you should:

options.text: Stop until the dog loses interest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach slowly, then speed up.
questions.explanation: Downshift and approach the dog slowly. Then accelerate and leave it behind.

questions.question: Motorists entering the highway from a ramp on your right may not see you. You should:

options.text: Move to the left side of your lane to let them share it.
Move to another lane if necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to another lane if necessary.
questions.explanation: Give plenty of room to vehicles merging from an entrance ramp. Change lanes away from the ramp if you can. If you cannot change lanes, slow down to make room for them to enter safely.

questions.question: When adjusting your mirrors, you should focus on:

options.text: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
The road in front of your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors to see the lane behind you and as much of the lane beside you as possible. A small part of your arm or shoulder in the mirror is okay, but the road behind and beside you is most important.

questions.question: When braking, what should you do?

options.text: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
Grab the front brake and squeeze the rear brake.
Jam on the front brake and grab the rear brake.
Press the front brake and jam the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
questions.explanation: To brake, squeeze the front brake lever and press the rear brake pedal. Always use both brakes when slowing or stopping.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding and you must stop, what should you do?

options.text: Relax your grip on the handlebars.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Use both brakes and stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, hold the handlebars firmly and ease off the throttle. Keep the motorcycle straight. If you must brake, apply it gently on the tire that is still good. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: When braking on a surface with poor traction, what should you do?

options.text: Apply the brakes harder than usual.
Do not use the rear brake.
Do not use the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the brakes gently.
questions.explanation: On surfaces with poor traction, apply the brakes gently. This helps you slow down safely without losing control.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding and you must stop, what is best to do?

options.text: Relax your grip on the handlebars.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Use both brakes and stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a tire fails, hold the handlebars firmly and slow down by easing off the throttle. Stay straight. If you must brake, apply it gently on the good tire if you are sure which one it is. Move to the side of the road as you slow down, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: When stopped behind another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Get as close as possible to the vehicle.
Keep a space between your motorcycle and the other vehicle.
Do not use your mirrors to check traffic behind you.
Look for ways to squeeze through stopped traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a space between your motorcycle and the other vehicle.
questions.explanation: Stay back from the vehicle in front of you, even when stopped. This gives you room to escape if the vehicle backs up or another vehicle comes too fast from behind.

questions.question: To swerve correctly, what should you do?

options.text: Press the handlebar in the direction you want to swerve.
Press the handlebar opposite the direction you want to swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handlebar in the direction you want to swerve.
questions.explanation: To avoid a hazard, press the handlebar in the direction you want to swerve. To swerve left, press the left handlebar, then press the right to straighten out. To swerve right, press the right handlebar, then the left.

questions.question: Helmeted riders are how many times more likely to survive a crash than riders without helmets?
questions.correctAnswerText: Three times
questions.explanation: At any speed, wearing a helmet makes you three times more likely to survive head injuries in a crash than without a helmet.

questions.question: If your front wheel skids while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Release the front brake and reapply it smoothly.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release both brakes and coast to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake and reapply it smoothly.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release the front brake right away and reapply it smoothly.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Hold the handlebars firmly and gradually close the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and gradually close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up, as this makes the wobble worse. Instead, hold the handlebars firmly, slow down by gradually closing the throttle, lean forward and down, and pull off the road as soon as you can. Avoid braking, as this can also make the wobble worse.

questions.question: When should you use a turn signal?

options.text: When you plan to speed up.
Only when there is heavy traffic.
Every time you plan to change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you plan to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Use a turn signal every time you plan to turn or change lanes, even if you think no one is watching.

questions.question: When riding in a group, why should inexperienced riders be placed near the front?

options.text: Experienced riders can watch them more easily.
They will get lost if they are leading.
They may slow the group down as leaders.
They will ride too fast in any other position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Experienced riders can watch them more easily.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride near the front, just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch them closely.

questions.question: If you find yourself riding next to another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Stay alongside until the next exit.
Let the other driver worry about it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up or slow down.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous. You could be in their blind spot. The vehicle could also block your escape route if a hazard appears. Speed up or drop back to get away from the vehicle.

questions.question: Most motorcycles have:

options.text: Brakes in both the front and rear.
Three brakes: front, rear, and emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brakes in both the front and rear.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have two brakes. One controls the front wheel. One controls the rear wheel.

questions.question: When riding near slow or stopped cars, what should a motorcyclist do?

options.text: Pull over and wait for traffic to move.
Ride on the shoulder to get through quickly.
Weave between cars to get through quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not weave between cars.
questions.explanation: Riding between slow or parked cars is dangerous. Car doors could open, or cars could suddenly pull into traffic. You won't have room to escape if a hazard appears. Never ride on the road shoulder because other drivers won't expect you there.

questions.question: What type of footwear is best for a motorcycle operator?
questions.correctAnswerText: Sturdy boots
questions.explanation: Sturdy boots or high shoes protect your ankles best. Laced-up boots work well. High-top boots or heavy shoes are also good. If your boots have long laces, tuck them in before riding.

questions.question: Where is the engine cut-off switch usually located?
questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right handgrip
questions.explanation: The engine cut-off switch is usually located next to the right handgrip. Know where all your motorcycle controls are before you start riding.

questions.question: What can you do to reduce your chances of crashing?

options.text: Use turn signals when changing lanes.
Focus your eyes only 15 feet ahead.
Don't use a headlight during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use turn signals when changing lanes.
questions.explanation: To reduce crashes, be visible to others. Tell other drivers what you plan to do. Keep enough space between you and other vehicles. Look ahead at least 12 seconds. Spot hazards early and stay ready to react.

questions.question: The body eliminates about one drink per hour. If someone drank eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks are likely still in their body?
questions.correctAnswerText: Four drinks
questions.explanation: Subtract the hours passed from the total drinks consumed. Eight drinks minus four hours equals about four drinks remaining in the body.

questions.question: As a motorcycle operator, how can you help others see you?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright clothing.
questions.explanation: To be seen better, wear bright clothing. Use your headlight at all times. Always use turn signals.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.
